parental_testing_statement.value: Whole-exome sequencing on patient 1 and his mother (patient 2), both carrying the heterozygous C243Y mutation. C243Y present in all familial patients with BD examined (all affected members apart from patient 6), absent in the proband's healthy younger brother and in 64 unrelated normal controls of the same Japanese ethnicity.

functional_evidence_statement.value: Mononuclear cells from patient 1 produced large amounts of IL-1β, IL-6 and TNF-α on LPS at various concentrations compared with normal controls (little difference for IL-8; no spontaneous production with medium alone). THP-1 cells transfected with C243Y A20: IL-1β, IL-6 and TNF-α secretions markedly less suppressed than with WT A20. HEK293T luciferase assay: suppression of Nod2-mediated NF-κB activation by C243Y A20 approximately two-thirds that of intact A20 at 33 ng; 333 ng of C243Y A20 completely attenuated NF-κB signalling; authors: variant 'does not cause complete loss of function, but, rather, causes weak function'. NLRP3 transcripts increased in C243Y-transfected THP-1 cells on stimulation, but patient 1's mononuclear cells did not display a remarkable increase of NLRP3 mRNA.

pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors.value: likely responsible for increased production of human inflammatory cytokines (Abstract); 'responsible for the autosomal-dominant inheritance of BD in this Japanese family' (Conclusion)
